newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Jan 3.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - The week favored sellers as buyers replenished inventories they had allowed to dwindle during December, Random Lengths said in its weekly market review. Prices finished mixed but gains outnumbered losses. Mills saw the week as the start of a post-holiday rally but many buyers still stood aside, it said.
Those buyers preferred to wait to see how the market reacts to a full week of production, Random Lengths said.

Unseasonably warm temperatures boosted consumption in parts of the Midwest, East and South. Meanwhile, storms caused slides, washouts and power outages that slowed production, shipments and logging from northern California to southern British Columbia.
A rapid climb in futures was a bullish sign for some traders. Western boards traded quietly but picked up a notch on Thursday; most shop and Mldg&Btr prices were unchanged.
Western S-P-F producers approached the market firmly, bolstered by hefty gains in futures and weather-hampered output.

Western S-P-F buyers were cautious, with most unwilling to place orders later than the week of Jan 13. Prices of Std&Btr 2x4 reported Thursday covered a wide range. Some sales were made early in the day at $395-400 but quotes reached $425 later in the day. Eastern S-P-F trading was slow, but the rise in futures and some inventory replenishment by dealers sparked early-week activity. The #1&2 2x4 gained $5, Random Lengths said.

The balance of Southern Pine tilted in favor of the mills after the holiday as limited stocks forced some buyers back to the market, Random Lengths said. Prices rose in response, with #2 2x8 leading the way. Random loadings of this width jumped $15 to $20 in the central and westside zones, the agency said.
